{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABbF4q4Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhEq_OY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 160, "title": "Simplify Graph Editor inspector, edge disconnection and migration recovery UI", "body": "## Problem

Graph Editor's Settings inspector currently appears only when a node is selected, changing the canvas width every time selection is cleared. Selecting an edge instead shows a large floating **Disconnect** button on the canvas, backed by elaborate overlap-placement logic. Finally, saved-graph migration/recovery backups are shown as an extra disclosure near the top of the page, even during normal editing.

These behaviors add unnecessary movement and visual clutter. The existing recovery **data** is important and must not be deleted.

## Expected outcome

Make three focused Graph Editor UX improvements using the existing UI; no new screen or framework.

### 1. Keep the inspector region stable

- On wide screens, keep the right-hand Settings/Details panel at a constant width, **including when nothing is selected**. Selection changes its contents, not the canvas dimensions.
- No selection: a minimal empty state. Node selection: existing node Settings, including the node ID. Edge selection: concise connection details and a **Disconnect** action.
- On narrow screens, keep the inspector below the canvas with similarly stable layout (without forcing an unusable full-height panel). Preserve canvas size/scroll position, node placement and keyboard focus when selection changes.
- Remove redundant "Close settings" behavior only if it no longer fits this model; preserve a straightforward way to clear selection and the existing Escape/blank-canvas interactions.

### 2. Simplify edge disconnection

- Allow a connected wire to be **detached by dragging its input endpoint into empty canvas space**. This is a direct manipulation alternative to the floating button; do not confuse it with the existing output-to-input connection drag.
- Keep selecting an edge then pressing Delete/Backspace. For touch and keyboard accessibility, show a clear Disconnect action **in the persistent inspector** when the edge is selected.
- Remove the oversized floating on-canvas Disconnect button and its specialized placement/overlap algorithm once the replacement paths work.
- Preserve existing click-to-connect, output dragging, occupied-input reconnection, fan-out, zoom/Fit, keyboard/touch, hit targets, and undo-free draft semantics. Detaching one wire must never remove other wires, connected nodes, or unrelated settings.
- Avoid creating a new permanent toolbar, hover-only action, gesture mode, or other controls.

### 3. Move migration recovery behind Graph actions

- Preserve **every existing exact saved-graph recovery copy** and the current reviewed migration/Save behavior, including the version-12 paired-input conversion and older numbered backups.
- In normal editing, put recovery-copy viewing/export/copy access in the **existing Graph actions** menu, under a succinct "Recovery" action/disclosure. Do not display the large "Original saved graph (migration recovery copy)" section near the top of the editor.
- When migration is blocking the graph from running, keep an **immediately visible, actionable warning** telling the user to review the repair draft and access the original under Graph actions → Recovery. Never hide an urgent problem or silently replace stored JSON.
- No new storage format, automatic migration acceptance, data deletion, recovery subsystem, or extra dialog required.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] At 1440px, selecting a node, edge and blank canvas preserves inspector width and graph viewport geometry; details change without layout jumps. At 390px, the editor remains usable without horizontal page overflow or obscuring the graph.
- [ ] Edge can be detached by dragging its input end to blank canvas. Click-to-connect, reconnection to another port, selecting a wire, Delete/Backspace, pointer and touch workflows continue to work. A selected wire is disconnectable through the inspector without a floating canvas button.
- [ ] Duplicate node types, node ID in Settings, keyboard focus recovery, zoom/Fit and saved draft graph behavior remain correct. No unintended graph changes on mere selection.
- [ ] Existing recovery copies remain byte-for-byte intact and reachable from Graph actions during normal operation and blocking migration. Invalid/old saved graphs retain their reviewed repair and original-backup protection; migration errors remain clearly visible.
- [ ] Focused Chromium/WebKit and packaged extension tests exercise desktop/narrow widths, selection transitions, drag-to-detach and alternate disconnection controls, recovery UI and saved graph integrity.
- [ ] Update directly affected editor documentation/tests only. Keep the change modest and consistent with "Keep it simple / Show, don't tell / Intuitive and predictable".

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Context

- `extension/graph-editor.js`: `drawInspector()`, `drawWires()`, `positionDisconnect()`, inspector and edge interactions.
- `extension/recorder.css`: `.graph-workspace.has-selection`, `.graph-inspector`, `#graph-disconnect`.
- `extension/graph-page.js`: original saved graph recovery disclosure.
- `extension/graph.js`: versioned migration and backup preservation.
- UI/UX principles in `README.md` and `docs/review-guidelines.md`; existing graph UX work #97, #109 and #151.
